title: A multisig must be registered and security-approved before it can appear in any Spell
content:
A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.8 makes registration a precondition rather than a record-keeping courtesy: all multisigs "currently in use or intended for use within Treasury Management, Emergency Operations ..., Capital Allocation, or Smart Contract Control ... must be registered prior to their inclusion in any Spell or governance execution process." The Administrator supplies the details to Core GovOps, and "Core GovOps must coordinate with the Protocol Security Workstream Lead to obtain approval prior to completing the registration."

Placing the gate at the Spell is what gives the whole framework teeth. Every other requirement in A.2.11.1.3 — classification, thresholds, module restrictions, signer security — is a duty owed by an administrator, enforceable only by discovering non-compliance after the fact. Registration is different: an unregistered multisig cannot receive authority through governance at all, because the only path to authority runs through a Spell.

This converts security compliance from an audit problem into an admission requirement, and it is why the Impact and Operational classifications must be supplied "as part of the Multisig registration process" — the assessment is the price of entry, not paperwork filed afterward.

The residual gap is scope. The gate binds multisigs receiving authority *via governance execution*. A multisig operating downstream of an already-authorized one, or funded by transfers rather than Spell-granted permissions, is not obviously caught by the same choke point.

Enforcement authority is also split by design: Core GovOps holds the registry, the Protocol Security Workstream Lead holds the approval, so neither can admit a multisig alone.
description: Treasury, emergency, capital allocation and contract-control multisigs must be registered with Core GovOps, with Protocol Security Workstream Lead approval, prior to inclusion in governance execution.
